title: Walk the Siq into the Treasury at Petra
description: A 1.2km slot canyon opens onto a facade carved into the rock face by the Nabataeans around 2,000 years ago. Go at opening, before the canyon fills.

title: Climb the 800 steps to the Monastery at Petra
description: Larger than the Treasury and far quieter, because most visitors stop before the climb. A tea shack at the top looks out over the Wadi Araba.

title: Sleep in a Bedouin camp in Wadi Rum
description: Sandstone and granite towers in red desert, run by Bedouin tribes who hold the tourism rights. Stood in for Mars in half a dozen films.

title: Float in the Dead Sea
description: 430m below sea level, the lowest land on earth, and about ten times saltier than the ocean. It is also shrinking by roughly a metre a year.

title: Walk the colonnaded street at Jerash
description: One of the best-preserved Roman provincial cities anywhere, buried by earthquake and sand until the 1920s - the oval forum is almost intact.

title: Walk the Dana Biosphere Reserve
description: Jordan's largest reserve, dropping 1,500m from highland to desert through four biogeographic zones, on a village-run conservation model.

title: Dive the Red Sea reefs at Aqaba
description: Jordan's only coastline, 27km of it, with reefs unusually resilient to bleaching and a deliberately sunk C-130 Hercules at 17m.

title: Go up the Burj Khalifa at sunset
description: 828m and still the tallest building in the world by a wide margin. Book the sunset slot weeks ahead - it is the only one that consistently sells out.

title: Ride a 4WD over the dunes on a desert safari
description: Dune bashing, sandboarding and a camp dinner in the Al Marmoom reserve. Genuinely rough - not a good idea straight after eating.

title: Haggle in the Dubai gold and spice souks
description: Reached by abra across Dubai Creek for about a dirham. Roughly ten tonnes of gold sits in the windows at any time, and the price is always negotiable.

title: Visit the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque
description: Holds 40,000 worshippers, with the largest hand-knotted carpet in the world on its floor. Free, and modest dress is provided at the entrance.

title: See the rain of light at Louvre Abu Dhabi
description: Jean Nouvel's 180m dome filters sun through eight layered star patterns, casting a shifting pattern of light on the galleries below.

title: Ride the world's longest zip line at Jebel Jais
description: 2.83km at up to 150km/h, flown head-first off the UAE's highest peak. The mountain road up is itself worth the drive.

title: Swim and climb through Wadi Shab
description: A boat across, 45 minutes on foot, then three pools to swim before squeezing through a crack in the rock to a waterfall inside a cave.

title: Walk the Balcony Walk on Jebel Shams
description: A ledge path along the rim of Wadi Ghul, called the Grand Canyon of Arabia, ending at an abandoned village cut into the cliff.

title: Camp in the Sharqiya Sands
description: Dunes up to 100m in bands of orange and white, still grazed by Bedouin herders. You let tyre pressure down at the edge and drive in.

title: Sail a dhow through the Musandam fjords
description: Sheer limestone inlets called the Norway of Arabia, on a peninsula separated from the rest of Oman by the UAE, with dolphins in the channels.

title: Go to the Friday goat market at Nizwa
description: Livestock paraded in a ring before dawn buyers, beside a 17th-century fort with a round tower built to survive cannon fire.

title: Watch green turtles nest at Ras al Jinz
description: One of the most important green turtle nesting sites in the Indian Ocean, with guided night and dawn visits from a reserve on the easternmost point of Arabia.

title: See Salalah green during the khareef
description: The monsoon turns a desert province green for three months a year - waterfalls, fog and the frankincense trees that made this coast rich.

title: Walk the Old City of Jerusalem
description: One square kilometre holding sites central to Judaism, Christianity and Islam. It sits in East Jerusalem, which most of the world regards as occupied territory.

title: Climb Masada for sunrise over the Dead Sea
description: A fortress on a desert plateau where a Jewish garrison held out against Rome until 73 CE. The Snake Path takes about an hour in the dark.

title: Float on the Sea of Galilee
description: Actually a freshwater lake, and the lowest on earth. The surrounding hills hold Capernaum and the Mount of Beatitudes.

title: Walk the Bauhaus White City in Tel Aviv
description: About 4,000 Bauhaus buildings put up by architects who fled Europe in the 1930s - the largest concentration anywhere, and World Heritage listed.

title: See Banksy's Walled Off Hotel in Bethlehem
description: A hotel built facing the separation wall, billed as having the worst view in the world, beside the Church of the Nativity. Entry is via Israeli checkpoint.

title: Walk the excavations at Jericho
description: Tell es-Sultan has evidence of settlement going back roughly 11,000 years, which makes it a contender for the oldest continuously inhabited place on earth.

title: Float over Cappadocia in a balloon at dawn
description: Up to 150 balloons lift at once over volcanic fairy chimneys. Flights are cancelled for wind more often than people expect - allow spare mornings.

title: Go down into the Derinkuyu underground city
description: Eighteen storeys cut into soft tuff, capable of sheltering 20,000 people with livestock, ventilation shafts and rolling stone doors.

title: Stand under the dome of the Hagia Sophia
description: Built as a cathedral in 537, converted to a mosque in 1453, a museum in 1935 and back to a mosque in 2020. Its dome went unmatched for a thousand years.

title: Get lost in the Grand Bazaar
description: Around 4,000 shops on 61 covered streets, trading since 1461 and among the oldest shopping complexes still operating anywhere.

title: Walk barefoot on the terraces at Pamukkale
description: White travertine terraces built by calcium-rich springs over millennia. Shoes are banned to protect them, and the Roman city of Hierapolis sits on top.

title: Walk the marble street at Ephesus
description: One of the largest Roman sites in the Mediterranean, with the Library of Celsus facade and a theatre that seated 25,000.

title: Watch sunrise among the heads on Mount Nemrut
description: Two-metre stone heads toppled from their bodies on a 2,134m summit, built as a tomb by a king who declared himself a god.

title: See the carved pillars at Gobekli Tepe
description: Monumental stone circles raised around 9500 BCE - roughly 6,000 years before Stonehenge, and by people who had not yet started farming.

title: See the Nabataean tombs at Hegra
description: Saudi Arabia's first World Heritage site - 111 tombs cut by the same civilisation that built Petra, and visited by a fraction of the numbers.

title: Stand at the Edge of the World near Riyadh
description: A 300m escarpment on the Tuwaiq cliffs where the plateau simply stops and an ancient seabed runs to the horizon. 4WD access only.

title: Walk the mud-brick city at Diriyah
description: At-Turaif, the original seat of the Saudi state, built in Najdi mud-brick and World Heritage listed since 2010.

title: Eat and haggle in Souq Waqif
description: Rebuilt in the traditional style on a centuries-old trading site, with a falcon souq and hospital in the middle of it.

title: See the collection at the Museum of Islamic Art
description: I M Pei came out of retirement at 91 to design it, on its own island so nothing could ever be built against it.

title: Drive to the inland sea at Khor Al Adaid
description: One of very few places on earth where the sea reaches into the heart of a desert, on the Saudi border and reachable only by 4WD across dunes.

title: Stand among the columns at Baalbek
description: The largest Roman temple complex ever built, with foundation stones over 800 tonnes that nobody has fully explained the moving of.

title: Take the boat through the Jeita Grotto
description: Two limestone caverns stacked over each other, the upper holding the largest known stalactite in the world at 8.2m, the lower toured by boat.

title: Walk the harbour at Byblos
description: Occupied for around 7,000 years and a candidate for the oldest continuously inhabited city. The Greek name for it gave us the word Bible.

title: Find the Tree of Life in the Bahraini desert
description: A mesquite standing alone in the desert for around 400 years with no obvious water source, roughly two kilometres from anything else.

title: Walk the layers at Qal'at al-Bahrain
description: A tell holding 4,000 years of continuous occupation, from the Dilmun civilisation up to a Portuguese fort on the top layer.

title: Go up the Kuwait Towers
description: Three towers finished in 1979, clad in eight million enamelled steel discs, badly damaged during the 1990 invasion and rebuilt afterwards.
